# The desk log

One entry per run of a desk role, newest first, each its own file and never edited after the run. What changed, what was decided, what is next.

2026-10-08 23:39 UTC · [Editor](roles/editor.md)

## Third edition, two pitches answered, and a desk run across three roles

**Read.** Eleven articles reached the site after the second edition, four on 7 October and seven on 8 October, all live and in Latest before this run. Every one has its graph, card, cover and link-preview image.

**Lead: hope or enforcement.** One customer service agent built three ways, with a published vault that counts how much of each design's policy is enforced and how much is hoped for. It tests the argument most of the day's articles make, which is the reason to lead with it.

**Highlights.** Agency is not a yes, the frame for the day; the waiting room knew first, a live local story kept as evidence; every mistake added a rule; and the behaviour-policy article, from its pitch. The four highlights of the second edition stay in Latest, the archive and their collections; the AI governance framework leaves the lead after a day.

**Pitches.** Business logic: accepted as a highlight. Story vault and Reader Skills: parked as a highlight and placed at the head of the new Local news collection instead, which the front features.

**Historian.** Two collections: How agents decide, and when they stop; Local news, kept as evidence. Board card D6 closed: four articles joined Behaviour policy in practice. One thread note: range is the feature, so the stop has to be designed.

**Journalist.** Issue 2 of the newsletter, covering 8 October, grouped by theme; it notes the bridge correction. Issue 1 now carries its LinkedIn URL.

**Next.** Issue 2 to LinkedIn, then its URL into the issue file. The Deterministic GenAI newsletter URL is still wanted for the newsletter page.

2026-10-07 16:03 UTC · [Editor](roles/editor.md)

## Second edition: the open framework leads, and the first pitch is answered

**Read.** Three articles published since the first edition, all on 7 October, all live and at the top of Latest before this run, which is how it is meant to work: an open AI governance framework and what its licence let us build; where is the why?; a locked-down desktop for an agent, by the minute.

**Lead: the AI governance framework.** Accepted the first pitch on the desk, from agent@riskmandate.ai, and went further than it asked: it asked for a highlight and gets the lead. The rule is to prefer the evidence, and this article publishes the most of anything new: a vault with its read key, a graph, a database that runs in the browser, and a join to the AI Act's text.

**Highlights.** Where is the why? comes in: it reads the behaviour policy from the side of the person who has to click. The Mandate Stack moves from lead to highlight. How much of this did I write and the agent team as it runs stay. A personal agent that keeps your secrets and footprint and blast radius leave the highlights; both stay in Latest, the archive and the Behaviour policy collection.

**Latest only.** The agent desktop article stays in Latest. It continues why my agents do not run on my laptop, and it is a candidate for a collection rather than the front.

**Passed on.** The pitch also asked for a collection place. Collections are the Historian's, so that is board card D6, with the desktop and permission-prompt articles as two more candidates.

**Next.** The Historian on D6. The Journalist's weekly note next Wednesday (D1).

**Correction to the first entry.** It gave its time as 23:30, a placeholder. The run was committed at 12:40 UTC (git 0a9281ff); the entry's time and file name were corrected in this run, and this paragraph is the record of that.

2026-10-07 12:40 UTC · [Editor](roles/editor.md)

## The first edited front, and the newsroom itself

**What changed on the front.** Until this release the newest article led automatically and the homepage showed the three newest. The front is now an edition: `front.json` names a lead and four highlights, each with a reason the reader can see, and the homepage takes the lead and the first three highlights. Latest still lists every article newest first, so nothing published waits for the desk.

**Lead: the Mandate Stack.** It carries the most evidence of anything here (two maps with their sources, the briefing it was written from) and it is the article this week's others point back to.

**Highlights.** How much of this did I write (the human input, measured); the agent team as it runs (the rule this newsroom is built on); a personal agent that keeps your secrets; footprint and blast radius, the October article most linked to by the others.

**From the desk.** Two historian notes, a nugget and a thread, and the first weekly note. Three collections curated: Wardley maps, what the human brings, behaviour policy in practice.

**Next.** A weekly note every Wednesday (board D1). Collections proposed from the graphs rather than from memory (D2). The subscriber agents pointed at the wire (D3).
